lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The 5:10 direct train has gone. We reached the platform at 5:13.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: If we’d left when the host gave the early-exit reminder at 4:05, we would’ve caught the 4:25 tram.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes, but at the time we didn’t know the final Q&A would continue until 4:15.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Looking back, staying until 4:18 left us only seven minutes to reach the tram stop.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I don’t regret hearing the last answer, but it had a transport consequence. We walked out at 4:20 and missed the tram.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The journey app shows that there was a 4:30 local bus from the stop beside the center.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That bus wasn’t on our paper map. If we’d checked the live board before leaving, we would’ve taken it.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: It was due here at 5:02, so it would have given us eight minutes for the connection.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That would have changed the result. Simply walking faster after 4:20 probably wouldn’t have been enough.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Agreed. The useful alternatives were leaving at 4:05 or checking live departures before we walked to the tram.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We should also record what we knew at the time. The printed program said the workshop ended at four.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And the paper map showed only the tram route. We chose that route with incomplete information.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It doesn’t help to blame either of us for not using a bus we didn’t know about.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Right. Still, we could have checked a live source when the session ran late.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s a fair process lesson. It’s different from saying one person caused the whole problem.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Let’s write it precisely: the Q&A overran, we left at 4:20, and our old map omitted the 4:30 bus.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then add the counterfactual: if we’d checked live departures at the door, we would’ve seen a workable connection.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: For the next trip, our trigger can be “ten minutes behind plan means check live options.”

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good. Now we need another way home, not another argument about the train that has already left.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I’ll open the current departure board, and we’ll compare the remaining routes against our actual priorities.
